name: REAP-S
fullName: Rapid Eating Assessment for Participants – Shortened
shortDescription: 13-item primary-care dietary quality screener tracking everyday nutrition habits (higher is healthier).
timeframe: In an average week, how often do you:
citation: Segal-Isaacson CJ, Wylie-Rosett J, Gans KM. Diabetes Educ. 2004;30(5):774-781; Johnston CS, et al. Nutrients. 2018;10(8):1095.

questions.text: Eat 4 or more meals from sit-down or take-out restaurants?

Eat less than 2 servings of whole grain products or high-fiber starches a day? (Serving = 1 slice 100% whole grain bread, 1 cup whole grain cereal/oatmeal, 3–4 whole grain crackers, or ½ cup brown rice/whole wheat pasta)
Eat less than 2 servings of fruit a day? (Serving = ½ cup or 1 medium fruit, or 4 oz 100% fruit juice)
Eat less than 2 servings of vegetables a day? (Serving = ½ cup cooked vegetables or 1 cup raw leafy vegetables)
Eat or drink less than 2 servings of milk, yogurt, or cheese a day? (Serving = 1 cup milk/yogurt or 1½–2 oz cheese)
Eat more than 8 ounces of meat, chicken, turkey, or fish per day? (3 oz ≈ size of a deck of cards)
Use regular processed meats (like bologna, salami, corned beef, hot dogs, sausage, or bacon) instead of low-fat processed meats (like roast beef, turkey, or lean ham)?
Eat fried foods such as fried chicken, fried fish, French fries, fried plantains, or fried yuca?
Eat regular potato chips, nacho chips, corn chips, crackers, or regular popcorn instead of pretzels, low-fat chips/crackers, or air-popped popcorn?
Add butter, margarine, or oil to bread, potatoes, rice, or vegetables at the table?
Eat sweets like cake, cookies, pastries, donuts, muffins, chocolate, and candies more than 2 times per day?
Drink 16 ounces or more of non-diet soda, fruit drink/punch, or sweetened beverages per day?

scoring.formulaDescription: Sum of all 13 dietary items (Usually/Often = 1, Sometimes = 2, Rarely/Never or Does not apply = 3; range 13–39). Higher scores indicate higher overall diet quality (mean ~32 in healthy adult cohorts).
